---

Probate records for Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania from the 1870s and 1880s were searched in FamilySearch's Pennsylvania Probate Records collection (spanning 1683 to 1994), looking for an estate filing by or for a Thomas Flynn that might name Patrick Flynn as a son. Only one Flynn probate record is indexed for that entire county across those 20 years — and it belongs to a completely different Patrick Flynn who died in May 1882 in Pottsville, not our Patrick (who died in 1908). Thomas Flynn's estate did not turn up at all, which almost certainly means the relevant probate volume has not been indexed and exists only as a page image that a text search cannot reach yet.

Next, the page images in the Pennsylvania probate collection will need to be searched using full-text tools that can scan un-indexed documents, since the indexed layer has been exhausted.

Logged as log_002. The record read reveals the full household picture. Here is the complete triage:

**Search:** log_002 — positive (1 result), 1860 US Census, collection 1473181, George Ackerman + spouse "Catherine" anchor, Pennsylvania

**Top match:** `ark:/61903/1:1:M7QZ-8KD`, matchScore 0.9412, not attached to subject I1. Cross-check: birth ~1818, Pennsylvania — consistent with the subject. Residence: Bucks County, Pennsylvania, 1860. No birth-year conflict.

The `relativeTerms.spouse` field returned `absent`, which the record read confirms: she is simply not in this household.

**Critical note on what the 1860 census shows about marriage:** The 1860 schedule collected names, ages, sex, occupation, birthplace, and real/personal property values — it did NOT collect a relationship-to-head column (that began in 1880). So there is no field on any 1860 record that labels someone a "wife" or states a marriage. Any marital relationship between household members listed together is an inference from surname, age, and listing order — not a stated fact. This record cannot confirm a marriage to Catherine in any case; it also happens not to list her at all.

**Ad-hoc search — no plan item to update.** The project already holds a separate source (src_001, record `M4QZ-7YT`) with 7 existing assertions, which likely represents the household record already extracted for this question.

No sources or assertions were created from this search; the result sits in the search log only.

A search was run in the 1860 United States federal census for George Ackerman of Pennsylvania, using his wife Catherine as a narrowing anchor. One strong match turned up, placing a George Ackerman in Bucks County, Pennsylvania, in 1860 alongside two others named Henry Ackerman and Margaret Ackerman. Catherine does not appear in this particular household at all. Crucially, the 1860 census schedule did not include a column for each person's relationship to the head of household — that detail was only added starting with the 1880 census — so no 1860 record of any kind will state that two people were married to each other; all you can say from the census is that people of the same surname shared a dwelling, and that the relationship is inferred from their ages and the order they were listed.
